utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-95-16-A, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Vladimir Santic, appeals procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour. I'm Upawansa Yapa, appearing for the Prosecution with Mr. Christopher Staker and Mr. Norman Farrell. Ms. Adele Erasmus is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Can I have the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my name is Ranko Radovic, I'm an attorney at law from Zagreb, and I'm appearing here on behalf of Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac, I'm an attorney at law, and I'm defending Mirjan Kupreskic in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Borislav Krajina; I'm an attorney at law from Sarajevo. My co-counsel is Mr. Zelimir Par, who is an attorney at law from Zagreb. Today we are appearing on behalf of the accused Vlatko Kupreskic. I have to inform Your Honour that yesterday the accused Vlatko Kupreskic cancelled the power of attorney for this case to me as his main counsel, and to Mr. Par as co-counsel. The Registry of the Tribunal has asked us to be present at this Status Conference nevertheless and to represent the accused Kupreskic until a further decision is made by the Registrar. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will take note of what you have just said. The Registry will therefore have to make a decision pursuant to the request made by the accused. Could the other counsel present themselves as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Luka Susak, I'm an attorney at law from Zagreb, and I am representing Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. My name is Petar Pavkovic, I'm an attorney at law from Zagreb, and I am representing Vladimir Santic, together with my colleague Mr. Mitko Vrdoljak, who is also an attorney at law from Zagreb. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. As you all know, this is a Status Conference which is being conducted for the first time in the appellate procedure in the Kupreskic case, pursuant to Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence -- I'm sorry, 65(B), or rather 65 bis. I am now going to read the relevant text: "An Appeals Chamber or an Appeals Chamber Judge shall convene a status conference, within one hundred twenty days of the filing of a notice of appeal and thereafter within one hundred twenty days after the last status conference, to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person." As the parties are probably familiar with, there has been an order issued by the Appeals Chamber recently whereby I have been designated as the pre-appeal Judge for this case. Let me remind you of the said order. The order in question was issued on the 16th of May, 2000, whereby a pre-appeal Judge was designated for this particular case. Of course, pursuant to Rule 65 ter of the Rules of Procedure, I will personally take care of the communication between the two parties during this pre-appeal phase of the procedure. The objective of this particular procedure is to achieve an expeditious and fair procedure as provided for by the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I will also take care of the time limits provided for by the Rules and also to envisage all the necessary measures that have to be taken so that the case can be prepared for a fair and expeditious proceeding. So far, you know that in accordance with the Rules, the party seeking to appeal the judgement must file a brief within a certain period of time which is provided for by the Rules, which is three months after the judgement. This is also provided for in the relevant Rules. Let me also remind you of the relevant provisions. One of the Rules that we're dealing with here is Rule 111, which regulates appellate's brief, and it has to be filed within 90 days of filing of the notice of appeal pursuant to Rule 108, and it has to contain both facts and legal arguments. Rule 108 provides as follows: "A party seeking to appeal a judgement shall not, more than fifteen days from the date at which the judgement was pronounced, file a notice of appeal." There has been already a request for extension of time limits by the appellant, and the Chamber has granted the motion of the appellant by extending the time limits in an order which was issued on the 18th of April. The time limit was extended until the 2nd of June, 2000. There has been a second request by the appellant, which was filed on the 25th of April, whereby the appellant has requested a further extension of time. The Prosecutor has responded to the motion filed by Defence, and the Chamber has made a decision issued on the 16th of May. It has decided to grant additional extension of time to the appellant, namely, to the 2nd of July, 2000, bearing in mind a number of considerations that have been exposed by the appellant and which are contained in the appellant's motion. I should like to hear whether on this particular issue, that is, the request filed by the appellant, which was followed by the decision which I just mentioned to you, the decision of the 16th of May, whether there is anything that you wish to say. I will give the floor to the Defence. I assume that you have been made familiar with the Appeals Chamber's decision of the 16th of May, 2000. Is there anything you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, having consulted my colleagues, I can say that so far we have no objections to this deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. I take it then that Mr. Radovic has spoken on behalf of the Defence team as a whole, and as far as I understand, you will be able to file your brief before the 2nd of July, 2000, so that we can continue with the procedure which is provided for in the Rules, which we need not be reminded of once again. As regards the elements of the case, I think that this is the only thing that the Chamber has been seized of so far. I should also like to say that the Prosecutor, if they also -- I should like to hear the Prosecutor whether they have anything to say at this Status Conference. Is there anything you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no matter to be raised at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, very much, Mr. Yapa. As regards the Defence -- Mr. Radovic, can he once again act as porte-parole for the Defence -- is there anything else the Defence wishes to raise at this point? Mr. Radovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Radovic. You know that I am here in my capacity of Pre-appeal Judge, and you can always contact me either through Mr. Hocking or directly to myself. You can always contact me concerning any matters that concern the Pre-appeal Judge. However, if there is anything that should be the matter of the Appeals Chamber as a whole, in that case, I will have to convey the relevant message to the Appeals Chamber in its full composition. Pursuant to the Rules, I now give the floor to the Defence but also to the accused who are present here in the courtroom. The accused may take the floor directly or they can express themselves through their counsel. I have to inquire here at this point about your health, physical and mental health, and about any other issues that you wish to raise concerning your detention conditions. I should also like to hear any questions, if you have any, again concerning the Rules of Detention. You know that the Rules provide that you can raise all relevant issues here during this conference. According to the Rules governing the detention procedure before the Tribunal, those questions need to be brought, first of all, before the relevant detention unit authorities. This is provided for in Rule 44, which says that the matters should be brought to the commander of the detention unit and also to the Registrar. However, of course you can bring all the necessary matters regarding your conditions of detention at this Status Conference. Mr. Radovic, is there anything that you wish to say? Do you wish to act as a porte-parole for your colleagues? As far as I can see, the accused do not intend to speak, and all I can conclude is that there are no questions at the moment that need to be raised and which concern the issues of mental or physical health of the accused. If there's nothing else that you wish to bring, I will adjourn this hearing, this Status Conference. Is there anything else that you wish to mention, aside from what I have already said? No? In that case, we will adjourn this hearing. You will, of course, be informed about the next Status Conference. If it is necessary, it can always be convened before the expiration of the time limits provided for in the Rules governing the appellate proceedings. The hearing stands adjourned.
